008package paint.ui.console;
009
010import paint.shared.utils.PaintLogger;
011
012import javax.swing.*;
013import javax.swing.text.*;
014import java.awt.*;
015import java.io.BufferedWriter;
016import java.io.File;
017import java.io.FileWriter;
018import java.io.IOException;
019import java.util.ArrayList;

024/**
025 * Provides a Swing-based console window for real-time message output.
026 * <p>
027 * Supports message coloring, saving logs to disk, problem highlighting,
028 * and scroll lock behavior.
029 */
030public final class PaintConsoleWindow {
031
032    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
033    // FIELDS
034    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
035
036    private static       JFrame         frame;
037    private static       JTextPane      textPane;
038    private static       StyledDocument doc;
039    private static       JCheckBox      scrollLock;
040    private static final List<Integer>  problemPositions = new ArrayList<>();
041    private static       int            currentProblemIndex = -1;
042
043    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
044    // PUBLIC LOGGING API
045    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
046
047    /**
048     * Adapter that lets {@link PaintLogger} feed this console without knowing it exists.
049     * Registered in {@link #createConsole(String)}, detached in {@link #close()}.
050     */
051    private static final PaintLogger.Sink CONSOLE_SINK = new PaintLogger.Sink() {
052        @Override
053        public void log(String line, Color color) {
054            PaintConsoleWindow.log(line, color);
055        }
056
057        @Override
058        public void print(String text) {
059            PaintConsoleWindow.print(text);
060        }
061    };
062
063    /**
064     * True when there is no display available — a headless pipeline run, a CI runner,
065     * or a server. Constructing any Swing component in that situation throws
066     * {@link HeadlessException}.
067     * <p>
068     * With the sink inversion this should be unreachable (a headless run never creates a
069     * console), but it is kept as a cheap belt-and-braces guard: the console is a GUI
070     * convenience only, and {@link PaintLogger} writes every line to the log file
071     * regardless, so doing nothing here loses no output.
072     */
073    private static boolean noDisplay() {
074        return GraphicsEnvironment.isHeadless();
075    }
076
077    /**
078     * Logs a message with a specified color. No-op when there is no display.
079     */
080    public static synchronized void log(String message, Color color) {
081        if (noDisplay()) {
082            return;
083        }
084        ensureConsoleCreated();
085        SwingUtilities.invokeLater(() -> appendText(message + "\n", color));
086    }
087
088    /**
089     * Prints a message in black text without newline.
090     */
091    public static synchronized void print(String message) {
092        print(message, Color.BLACK);
093    }
094
095    /**
096     * Prints a message with the specified color without newline. No-op when there is no display.
097     */
098    public static synchronized void print(String message, Color color) {
099        if (noDisplay()) {
100            return;
101        }
102        ensureConsoleCreated();
103        SwingUtilities.invokeLater(() -> appendText(message, color));
104    }
105
106
107    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
108    // WINDOW CONTROL
109    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
110
111    /**
112     * Closes and disposes of the console window, clearing all references and data.
113     * Also detaches this console from {@link PaintLogger}, so nothing tries to render
114     * into a window that no longer exists.
115     */
116    public static synchronized void close() {
117        disposeConsole();
118    }
119
120    /**
121     * Attaches automatic console closure when a given dialog is disposed.
122     */
123    public static void closeOnDialogDispose(JDialog dialog) {
124        dialog.addWindowListener(new java.awt.event.WindowAdapter() {
125            @Override
126            public void windowClosed(java.awt.event.WindowEvent e) {
127                close();
128            }
129        });
130    }
131
132    /**
133     * Closes the console window if it is currently on screen.
134     */
135    public static synchronized void closeIfVisible() {
136        if (frame != null && frame.isDisplayable()) {
137            disposeConsole();
138        }
139    }
140
141    /**
142     * Detaches this console from {@link PaintLogger} and disposes the window.
143     * <p>
144     * Both {@link #close()} and {@link #closeIfVisible()} route through here. They used to carry
145     * their own copy of this teardown, and the copies drifted: {@code closeIfVisible()} disposed
146     * the frame without clearing the sink, so the logger kept feeding a window that no longer
147     * existed — and the next log line simply popped a fresh one. Clearing the sink must happen
148     * whenever the window goes away, so it happens in exactly one place.
149     */
150    private static void disposeConsole() {
151        PaintLogger.clearSink();
152
153        if (frame == null) {
154            return;
155        }
156        SwingUtilities.invokeLater(() -> {
157            frame.setVisible(false);
158            frame.dispose();
159            frame = null;
160            textPane = null;
161            doc = null;
162            scrollLock = null;
163            problemPositions.clear();
164            currentProblemIndex = -1;
165        });
166    }
167
168    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
169    // TITLE MANAGEMENT
170    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
171
172    /**
173     * Sets the title of the console window.
174     */
175    public static synchronized void setConsoleTitle(String title) {
176        if (frame != null) {
177            SwingUtilities.invokeLater(() -> frame.setTitle(title != null ? title : "Paint Console"));
178        }
179    }
180
181    /**
182     * Creates or updates the console window for a specific creator name.
183     * No-op when there is no display.
184     */
185    public static synchronized void createConsoleFor(String creatorName) {
186        if (noDisplay()) {
187            return;
188        }
189        if (frame == null) {
190            createConsole("Paint Console – " + (creatorName != null ? creatorName : "Unknown"));
191        } else {
192            setConsoleTitle("Paint Console – " + (creatorName != null ? creatorName : "Unknown"));
193        }
194    }
195
196    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
197    // INTERNAL CONSOLE CREATION
198    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
199
200    private static void ensureConsoleCreated() {
201        if (frame == null) {
202            createConsole();
203        }
204    }
205
206    private static void createConsole() {
207        createConsole("Paint Console");
208    }
209
210    /**
211     * Creates and displays the console window with default components and layout,
212     * and attaches it to {@link PaintLogger} as the output sink.
213     * <p>
214     * This registration is what keeps the dependency pointing the right way: the logger
215     * knows nothing about Swing, and the console opts in. A headless run never creates a
216     * console, so it never registers a sink and never loads a UI class.
217     */
218    private static void createConsole(String title) {
219        PaintLogger.setSink(CONSOLE_SINK);
220
221        frame = new JFrame(title != null ? title : "Paint Console");
222        frame.setSize(1200, 400);
223        frame.setDefaultCloseOperation(WindowConstants.DISPOSE_ON_CLOSE);
224        frame.setLayout(new BorderLayout());
225
226        textPane = new JTextPane();
227        textPane.setEditable(false);
228        textPane.setFont(new Font(Font.MONOSPACED, Font.PLAIN, 12));
229        doc = textPane.getStyledDocument();
230
231        DefaultCaret caret = (DefaultCaret) textPane.getCaret();
232        caret.setUpdatePolicy(DefaultCaret.NEVER_UPDATE);
233
234        JScrollPane scrollPane = new JScrollPane(textPane);
235
236        // Smooth scrolling
237        scrollPane.getVerticalScrollBar().setUnitIncrement(20);
238        scrollPane.getHorizontalScrollBar().setUnitIncrement(20);
239
240        JPanel controlPanel = new JPanel(new BorderLayout());
241        scrollLock = new JCheckBox("Scroll Lock");
242        scrollLock.addActionListener(e -> updateTitleForScrollLock(scrollLock.isSelected()));
243        controlPanel.add(scrollLock, BorderLayout.WEST);
244
245        JPanel buttonPanel      = new JPanel(new FlowLayout(FlowLayout.RIGHT));
246        JButton highlightButton = new JButton("Highlight Problems");
247        highlightButton.addActionListener(e -> highlightProblemsOrNext());
248        JButton saveButton  = new JButton("Save");
249        JButton closeButton = new JButton("Close");
250        saveButton.addActionListener( e -> PaintConsoleWindow.saveConsoleContent());
251        closeButton.addActionListener(e -> close());
252
253        buttonPanel.add(highlightButton);
254        buttonPanel.add(saveButton);
255        buttonPanel.add(closeButton);
256        controlPanel.add(buttonPanel, BorderLayout.EAST);
257
258        frame.add(scrollPane, BorderLayout.CENTER);
259        frame.add(controlPanel, BorderLayout.SOUTH);
260        frame.setLocationRelativeTo(null);
261        frame.setVisible(true);
262    }
263
264    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
265    // TEXT HANDLING AND SAVING
266    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
267
268    /**
269     * Appends colored text to the console.
270     */
271    private static void appendText(String text, Color color) {
272        try {
273            Style style = textPane.addStyle("Style", null);
274            StyleConstants.setForeground(style, color);
275            doc.insertString(doc.getLength(), text, style);
276
277            if (!scrollLock.isSelected()) {
278                textPane.setCaretPosition(doc.getLength());
279            }
280        } catch (BadLocationException e) {
281            e.printStackTrace();
282        }
283    }
284
285    /**
286     * Saves console output to a user-selected file.
287     */
288    private static void saveConsoleContent() {
289        JFileChooser chooser = new JFileChooser();
290        chooser.setDialogTitle("Save Console Output");
291        int choice = chooser.showSaveDialog(frame);
292        if (choice == JFileChooser.APPROVE_OPTION) {
293            File file = chooser.getSelectedFile();
294            try (BufferedWriter writer = new BufferedWriter(new FileWriter(file))) {
295                writer.write(textPane.getText());
296                JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(frame, "Console saved to " + file.getAbsolutePath());
297            } catch (IOException ex) {
298                JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(frame,
299                                              "Failed to save file:\n" + ex.getMessage(),
300                                              "Error", JOptionPane.ERROR_MESSAGE);
301            }
302        }
303    }
304
305    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
306    // PROBLEM HIGHLIGHTING AND NAVIGATION
307    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
308
309    /**
310     * Highlights detected problems in the console output or navigates to the next highlighted problem.
311     * <p>
312     * This method performs two primary actions:
313     * 1. If no problems have been highlighted yet, it identifies problems in the text output
314     * (e.g., errors, warnings, exceptions) and highlights them.
315     * 2. If problems are already highlighted, it navigates to the next problem in the list,
316     * looping back to the first problem when the end of the list is reached.
317     * <p>
318     * Behavior:
319     * - If the scroll lock button is present and not already selected, it is activated to
320     * ensure that the highlighting and navigation operate properly.
321     * - Problems are identified using a predefined pattern (e.g., "Error", "Warning", "Exception").
322     * - If no problems are found during the initial search, a dialog is displayed informing
323     * the user that no issues were detected.
324     * - Navigation across detected problems is cyclical, wrapping around to the first
325     * problem after reaching the last one.
326     * <p>
327     * Thread Safety:
328     * This method is not explicitly synchronized and may require synchronization if called
329     * in a multithreaded environment to ensure that shared state (such as problemPositions
330     * and currentProblemIndex) is safely updated.
331     * <p>
332     * Effects:
333     * - Updates the scroll lock state and the console title if necessary.
334     * - Highlights newly identified problem areas in the console output.
335     * - Modifies the `currentProblemIndex` to track the currently selected problem.
336     */
337    private static void highlightProblemsOrNext() {
338        if (scrollLock != null && !scrollLock.isSelected()) {
339            scrollLock.setSelected(true);
340            updateTitleForScrollLock(true);
341        }
342
343        if (problemPositions.isEmpty()) {
344            // First click: find and highlight
345            highlightProblems();
346            if (!problemPositions.isEmpty()) {
347                currentProblemIndex = 0;
348                selectProblem(problemPositions.get(currentProblemIndex));
349            } else {
350                JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(frame, "No problems found (error, warning, exception).");
351            }
352        } else {
353            // Subsequent clicks: move to next match
354            currentProblemIndex++;
355            if (currentProblemIndex >= problemPositions.size()) {
356                currentProblemIndex = 0; // wrap around
357            }
358            selectProblem(problemPositions.get(currentProblemIndex));
359        }
360    }
361
362    /**
363     * Highlights problems in the console output based on predefined patterns.
364     * <p>
365     * This method scans the console's text content and highlights specific terms
366     * that indicate potential problems, such as "error", "warning", and "exception".
367     * The method uses regular expressions to identify these terms, including
368     * variations in capitalization and tolerance for ANSI color codes.
369     * <p>
370     * The detected terms are highlighted with different colors:
371     * - "Error" and "Exception" are highlighted in pink.
372     * - "Warning" and "Warn" are highlighted in orange.
373     * <p>
374     * Detected problem positions are stored in a list for further navigation or processing.
375     * <p>
376     * Functionality:
377     * - Removes all existing highlights before applying new ones.
378     * - Clears the previously recorded problem positions and resets the current
379     * problem index to indicate no problem is currently selected.
380     * - Performs a case-insensitive search, tolerating leading/trailing spaces
381     * and ANSI formatting codes.
382     * - Marks detected terms with appropriate highlight colors.
383     * - Adds the start position of each detected problem to the list for future reference.
384     * <p>
385     * Design notes:
386     * - The method is private and applies highlights within the text pane associated
387     * with the console.
388     * - If an exception occurs while applying highlights (due to invalid positions),
389     * it is logged but does not interrupt execution.
390     * <p>
391     * Thread Safety:
392     * This method is not thread-safe and should be externally synchronized if
393     * accessed from multiple threads, as shared structures like problemPositions
394     * and currentProblemIndex are modified.
395     */
396    private static void highlightProblems() {
397        Highlighter highlighter = textPane.getHighlighter();
398        highlighter.removeAllHighlights();
399        problemPositions.clear();
400        currentProblemIndex = -1;
401
402        // Get full text as-is
403        String fullText = textPane.getText();
404
405        // Unified regex to catch most variants: ERROR, Error, WARN, Warning, etc.
406        // Also tolerates ANSI color codes (\u001B[...]m) and leading/trailing spaces.
407        Pattern pattern = Pattern.compile(
408                "(?i)(?:\\u001B\\[[;\\d]*m)?\\b(?:error|warn|warning|exception)\\b(?:\\u001B\\[[;\\d]*m)?"
409        );
410
411        Matcher matcher = pattern.matcher(fullText);
412        while (matcher.find()) {
413            try {
414                String match = matcher.group().toLowerCase();
415                Color color = match.contains("error") || match.contains("exception")
416                        ? Color.PINK : Color.ORANGE;
417
418                highlighter.addHighlight(
419                        matcher.start(),
420                        matcher.end(),
421                        new DefaultHighlighter.DefaultHighlightPainter(color)
422                );
423                problemPositions.add(matcher.start());
424            } catch (BadLocationException e) {
425                e.printStackTrace();
426            }
427        }
428    }
429
430
431    /**
432     * Highlights and selects a specific text region in a text pane based on the given position.
433     * This method applies a yellow highlight to the specified region and sets the text caret within the region,
434     * making the region both focused and visible. Previous focus highlights are cleared before applying the new one.
435     *
436     * @param pos the starting position of the text region to be highlighted and selected
437     */
438    private static void selectProblem(int pos) {
439        try {
440            Highlighter highlighter = textPane.getHighlighter();
441            Highlighter.HighlightPainter focusPainter = new DefaultHighlighter.DefaultHighlightPainter(Color.YELLOW);
442
443            for (Highlighter.Highlight h : highlighter.getHighlights()) {
444                if (h.getStartOffset() == pos) {
445                    textPane.requestFocus();
446                    textPane.setCaretPosition(h.getEndOffset());
447                    textPane.select(h.getStartOffset(), h.getEndOffset());
448                    highlighter.addHighlight(h.getStartOffset(), h.getEndOffset(), focusPainter);
449                    textPane.scrollRectToVisible(textPane.modelToView(h.getStartOffset()));
450                    return;
451                }
452            }
453        } catch (BadLocationException e) {
454            e.printStackTrace();
455        }
456    }

462    /**
463     * Updates window title to reflect scroll lock state.
464     */
465    private static void updateTitleForScrollLock(boolean locked) {
466        if (frame == null) {
467            return;
468        }
469        String baseTitle = frame.getTitle().replace(" [Scroll Locked]", "");
470        frame.setTitle(locked ? baseTitle + " [Scroll Locked]" : baseTitle);
471    }
